specificity.explanation: Delivers a duration figure, a percentage change and a base year, though the sentence is garbled enough in delivery that which quantity rose by 49 percent is not fully pinned down.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: What I announced today is that we now have 70,000 people in case management with independent, individual employment plans.
specificity.explanation: A single precise count attached to a named mechanism (case management with individual employment plans) that could be checked against MSD reporting.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Does she think it is reasonable to cut jobseeker for young people when over 218 applications for one role at a Tank Juice bar show that there are simply no jobs available?
specificity.explanation: Names the policy change, an exact application count and the employer concerned — concrete enough for anyone to go and check.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: But as my colleague Mr Bishop has said, over $60 billion has been put aside for infrastructure, including the construction sector, over the next four years.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Government has allocated more than $60 billion to infrastructure across the coming four years.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury Budget 2025 capital allowance figures and the National Infrastructure Plan / Infrastructure Pipeline totals for the four years from 2025/26; true if the committed infrastructure capital exceeds $60 billion over that window, false if materially lower or if the figure covers a different period.

veracity.statement: Well, given that the size of our economy is $440-odd billion, it takes a while to turn the super-tanker around.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand's economy is approximately $440 billion in size.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ nominal GDP (annual, current prices) for the year to June 2025; true if in the range ~$430-450 billion, false if materially outside it.

veracity.statement: How can she stand by her statement that “We have invested more in public infrastructure.”, when there are 20,000 fewer people working in construction?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that construction employment has fallen by about 20,000 people.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ Household Labour Force Survey / filled jobs series for the construction industry, comparing the September 2025 quarter with the level at the change of government (December 2023 quarter); true if the fall is approximately 20,000, false if materially smaller or if employment rose.

veracity.statement: Half of teachers reported that students’ English and maths have improved compared to last year.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Education Review Office's report found approximately 50 percent of teachers reporting improved student achievement in English and maths year-on-year.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The ERO evaluation of the English and maths curriculum implementation released 15 October 2025; true if the report records approximately half of surveyed teachers reporting improvement, false if the figure is materially different or measures something other than year-on-year improvement.

veracity.statement: Nearly 80 percent of primary teachers have accessed professional learning and development in delivering structured literacy, and ERO found that teachers who used the 1.1 million maths books, textbooks, workbooks, and teacher guides that we have delivered were four times more likely to change their teaching practice.
veracity.explanation: Asserts an ~80 percent PLD uptake among primary teachers, delivery of 1.1 million maths resources, and an ERO finding of a fourfold difference in changed teaching practice among users of those resources.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Education PLD participation records for structured literacy and the October 2025 ERO report; true if all three figures appear at approximately those values, false if the uptake, the resource count or the fourfold ratio is materially different or not in the report.

veracity.statement: Very exciting announcement: three new charter schools announced this week so far, taking the total number to 14, with more to come later in the week.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that three charter schools were announced in the week to 15 October 2025 and that the cumulative total of announced charter schools is 14.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Charter School Agency / Ministry of Education list of approved charter schools and the Associate Minister's announcements to 15 October 2025; true if the announced total stands at 14, false if the register shows a materially different count.

veracity.statement: Because under their watch, the number of young people that went on to benefit under the age of 25—the duration increased to 18 future years on welfare, a 49 percent increase since 2017.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the average projected future years on welfare for beneficiaries aged under 25 reached 18 years, and that this represents a 49 percent increase since 2017.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MSD Benefit System Performance Report / valuation of the benefit system, average future years on main benefit for the under-25 cohort, 2017 versus the most recent valuation; true if the figure is approximately 18 years and the increase from 2017 is approximately 49 percent, false if either number is materially different.

veracity.statement: What I announced today is that we now have 70,000 people in case management with independent, individual employment plans.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that 70,000 beneficiaries are currently in MSD case management, each with an individual employment plan.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MSD case management and employment plan statistics as at the October 2025 announcement; true if the caseload is approximately 70,000 with individual plans, false if the count is materially lower or if the plans are not individually held.

veracity.statement: So, despite it being challenging, we’re seeing more people exit the jobseeker benefit into jobs, including 14.4 percent under the age of 25.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that jobseeker exits into employment have risen year-on-year, with a stated 14.4 percent figure relating to those under 25.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MSD quarterly benefit fact sheets on jobseeker support cancellations into work, September 2025 quarter compared with September 2024; true if exits into work rose year-on-year and the under-25 figure matches 14.4 percent, false if exits fell or the figure is materially different.

veracity.statement: Does she think it is reasonable to cut jobseeker for young people when over 218 applications for one role at a Tank Juice bar show that there are simply no jobs available?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that more than 218 applications were received for a single advertised role at a Tank Juice outlet.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Contemporaneous news reporting of the Tank Juice vacancy or a statement from the employer; true if the reported application count for one role is 218 or more, false if materially fewer or if the figure covers multiple roles.

veracity.statement: Who is correct: the Prime Minister, who said that young people need to get off the couch, stop playing PlayStation, and go and find a job, or Student Job Search chief executive Louise Saviker, who said applications are outpacing job listings?
veracity.explanation: Relays two attributed statements: that the Prime Minister told young people to get off the couch and stop playing PlayStation, and that Student Job Search's chief executive said applications are outpacing listings. What is at issue is whether each was said as characterised.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: Media transcripts or recordings of the Prime Minister's remarks about young jobseekers, and reporting of Louise Saviker's comments for Student Job Search; true if both were said substantially as quoted, false if either is misattributed or materially altered in the paraphrase.

focus.statement: We are not only very focused on the right navigational bearings but we’re leaving the storm and hurricane of destruction that was left to us by the last regime.
focus.explanation: Entirely metaphor about the previous government's general record. No policy, measure, figure or outcome is named — nothing here could be checked or acted on.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: How can she stand by her statement that “We have invested more in public infrastructure.”, when there are 20,000 fewer people working in construction?
focus.explanation: Legitimate scrutiny: quotes a specific ministerial claim and sets a specific measured outcome against it. Naming both the commitment and the counter-evidence is exactly the accountability case that must score high.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Who else is there to blame for her economic mismanagement, given that since she was asked this question last week, her Government has added teachers, firefighters, doctors, nurses, and the unions to that list?
focus.explanation: The substance is who the Government is blaming rather than any named policy, figure or outcome; the list of occupations is party framing, not a policy point.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: That was an education secretary under a Labour Minister, Peter Fraser, and I would love to see the Labour Party fulfil that kind of aspiration for the students of New Zealand rather than cuddle up to the unions.
focus.explanation: There is a real point about educational aspiration, but the weight of the sentence is a claim about what Labour is really like and whose interests it serves. No policy, figure or outcome is named on either side of the contrast.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: They’re both correct, because what we do know is that we have a higher aspiration for young people, clearly, than the Opposition do.
focus.explanation: A comparison of the two parties' aspirations. No policy, mechanism, figure or outcome appears in the sentence at all.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Will she admit that instead of doing her job, she’s kicking 18- and 19-year-olds off jobseeker because she’s failing to get to her 50,000 jobseeker reduction target?
focus.explanation: Names the specific measure (removing 18- and 19-year-olds from jobseeker support) and the specific commitment it is set against (the 50,000 reduction target). Scrutiny of a named target, not party-bashing, though the motive framing pulls it slightly off the policy.
focus.subject: speaker

civility.statement: We are not only very focused on the right navigational bearings but we’re leaving the storm and hurricane of destruction that was left to us by the last regime.
civility.explanation: "The last regime" and "storm and hurricane of destruction" are aimed at a former government, not at any individual member. Pointed and loaded, but it lands on no person.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Who else is there to blame for her economic mismanagement, given that since she was asked this question last week, her Government has added teachers, firefighters, doctors, nurses, and the unions to that list?
civility.explanation: Goes past the record and imputes a pattern of bad faith — that the Minister deflects blame onto whoever is at hand. Short of a direct insult, but the target has shifted from the policy to the person's conduct.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Will she admit that instead of doing her job, she’s kicking 18- and 19-year-olds off jobseeker because she’s failing to get to her 50,000 jobseeker reduction target?
civility.explanation: "Instead of doing her job" and the imputed motive — cutting young people off to cover a missed target — attribute bad faith to the Minister personally rather than contesting the policy on its merits.
civility.subject: speaker

divination.statement: That’s why we had 58 different applications for people to run new schools in this round, and I’m very much looking forward to announcing even more of these new schools as well as a growing number of State schools converting to charter status as the year completes.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that the number of existing State schools converting to charter status will grow over the remainder of 2025. The conversion decision rests with each school's board and community, so this is a forecast about others' behaviour rather than a promise about the speaker's own action.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: The Charter School Agency / Ministry of Education register of converted State schools; true if more State schools have completed or been approved for conversion by 31 December 2025 than had done so at 15 October 2025, false if the count is unchanged.

veracity.statement: We had violent crime up 33 percent, gang membership up 51 percent; we had a four-fold increase in ram raids, and a doubling of retail crime.
veracity.explanation: Asserts four specific changes in crime measures over the period of the previous government: violent crime +33%, gang membership +51%, ram raids up four-fold, retail crime doubled.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Crime and Victims Survey violent-victimisation figures and Police National Gang List membership counts for 2017-2023, plus Police ram-raid and retail-crime offence series; true if each of the four figures is within rounding of the stated change, false if any is materially different.

veracity.statement: I’m proud to say there are 29,000 fewer victims of serious violent crime; there’s a 16 percent reduction in serious youth offending.
veracity.explanation: Two claims about change under the current government: 29,000 fewer victims of serious violent crime, and a 16 percent fall in serious youth offending.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Crime and Victims Survey victim-count change for serious violent offences between the 2023 and 2025 cycles, and Police/Oranga Tamariki serious youth offending statistics for the same period; true if both figures match within rounding, false otherwise.

veracity.statement: I consider that the member who was the education Minister for 5½ years did a pretty bad job, actually, making sure that over half our kids weren't at school regularly and that half of them couldn't read at the standard they needed to be going into high school, and 80 percent weren’t at the standard they needed in maths.
veracity.explanation: Three claims about the state of education at the end of the previous government: over half of pupils not regularly attending, half not reading at the required standard entering high school, 80 percent below the maths standard.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Education regular-attendance data for 2022-23 and the curriculum-benchmark studies of Year 8 reading and mathematics achievement; true if each of the three proportions is within rounding of the published figures, false if any is materially overstated.

veracity.statement: We didn't increase it 84 percent. We didn't triple the debt to $180 billion, writing out a $9 billion interest rate bill.
veracity.explanation: Attributes to the previous government an 84 percent increase in government spending, a tripling of debt to $180 billion, and a $9 billion annual interest cost.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury core Crown expenses for 2017/18 vs 2022/23, gross sovereign-issued/net core Crown debt over the same period, and the Crown finance-cost line in the most recent fiscal update; true if spending rose about 84%, debt roughly tripled to about $180b, and finance costs are about $9b, false if any is materially different.

veracity.statement: We have had record farmer confidence, we have had 12 percent growth in our exports overseas, and our primary industry sectors are doing very well.
veracity.explanation: Claims farmer confidence is at a record level and that exports have grown 12 percent.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Federated Farmers/Rabobank rural confidence survey series as at late 2025 (true only if the reading is the highest on record), and Stats NZ goods-export values for the year to September 2025; true if annual export growth is about 12%, false if materially lower.

veracity.statement: Just yesterday, you would have seen 86 percent confidence in our tourism operators—our second biggest industry, at 7.5 percent of our total GDP.
veracity.explanation: Claims a tourism-operator confidence reading of 86 percent published on 14 October 2025, and that tourism is New Zealand's second-largest industry at 7.5 percent of GDP.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The tourism industry confidence survey released on 14 October 2025 (true if the headline figure is 86%), and the Stats NZ Tourism Satellite Account for tourism's share of GDP and its rank among industries; true if tourism is second-largest at about 7.5% of GDP, false if the share or rank is materially different.

veracity.statement: But what Kiwis are sick of is unions prioritising their interests ahead of kids who haven't been in school, the kids that are about to go into exams over the next wee while, the tens of thousands of patients that have been waiting because they ran up the wait-list like 20 times since they were in power.
veracity.explanation: Claims the health waiting list grew roughly twentyfold under the previous government.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Health New Zealand / Ministry of Health elective surgery and first-specialist-assessment waiting list counts for 2017 and 2023; true if the list grew by roughly a factor of twenty, false if the growth was materially smaller.

veracity.statement: We supported the initial pay equity legislation that came through the House, but that member took a paper to Cabinet and blew the cost from $3.5 billion up to $12 to $13 billion.
veracity.explanation: Claims the member took a Cabinet paper that raised the fiscal cost of the pay equity regime from $3.5 billion to $12-13 billion.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Released Cabinet papers and Treasury/Public Service Commission costings of pay equity claims under the 2017-2023 government; true if a paper taken by that Minister is shown to have moved the estimated cost from about $3.5b to about $12-13b, false if no such paper exists or the costings do not move as described.

veracity.statement: Does he stand by his statement on becoming Prime Minister two years ago, “We’re desperate to get to work to try and make things better for New Zealanders.”; if so, why do twice as many New Zealanders think things will be the same or worse in the next 12 months compared to those who think things will get better?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that twice as many New Zealanders expect the next 12 months to be the same or worse as expect improvement.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Published New Zealand polling on the 12-month outlook current in October 2025 (e.g. Ipsos Issues Monitor, consumer confidence outlook series); true if the same-or-worse share is about double the better share, false if the ratio is materially smaller.

veracity.statement: So why is he willing to accept a pay rise in line with inflation, claim a $50,000 housing allowance, and spend $44,000 on a helicopter ride so he could take a photograph for his Facebook, while his Government makes pay offers to workers like firefighters, nurses, and teachers that amount to pay cuts in real terms?
veracity.explanation: Asserts three specific facts about the Prime Minister's own entitlements and spending: a pay rise in line with inflation, a $50,000 housing allowance, and $44,000 spent on a helicopter trip.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Remuneration Authority determinations on parliamentary salaries and the Prime Minister's accommodation entitlement, and the published ministerial expense disclosures covering the helicopter flight; true if the allowance is about $50,000 and the flight cost about $44,000, false if materially different or not claimed.

veracity.statement: If his Government is so supportive of pay equity, how many of the 33 active pay equity claims that were in the process when he became Prime Minister have been settled during his two years as Prime Minister?
veracity.explanation: Asserts there were 33 active pay equity claims in process at the time the current Prime Minister took office.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Public Service Commission / MBIE records of pay equity claims lodged and unresolved as at late November 2023; true if the count is 33, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: From this month, women aged 70 and 74 are now eligible for free breast screening—the first step in the Government’s nationwide age extension for all women aged between 70 and 74.
veracity.explanation: Claims that eligibility for free breast screening extended to women aged 70 and 74 from October 2025, as the first stage of an extension to all women aged 70-74.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: BreastScreen Aotearoa / Health New Zealand published eligibility criteria and the associated ministerial announcement; true if the age-70 and age-74 cohorts became eligible in October 2025, false if the start date or the cohorts differ.

veracity.statement: The actual truth of the matter is that with the reduction and the improvement in terms of monetary policy, more liquidity is coming into the economy, banks are more confident, and the market is talking about yet another further reduction in monetary policy standards from 2.5 percent to some other figure.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the official cash rate stands at 2.5 percent and that market expectations are for a further cut from that level.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: RBNZ Official Cash Rate as at 15 October 2025 and contemporaneous market pricing/bank economist forecasts for the next review; true if the OCR is 2.5% and a further cut was being priced, false if the rate differs or no further cut was expected.

veracity.statement: How can she stand by her statement that she is, “making changes that will set our country up for a better future”, when 200 Kiwis a day do not see a better future and are choosing to leave the country?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that 200 New Zealanders a day are leaving the country.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ international migration estimates for New Zealand citizen departures / net citizen migration loss over the year to mid-2025; true if the figure averages about 200 a day (roughly 73,000 a year) on the measure used, false if materially lower.

veracity.statement: How can she stand by her statement in April this year that “We’ve been seeing green shoots across the economy.”, when at that time the economy was shrinking by almost 1 percent?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that as at April 2025 the economy was contracting by almost 1 percent.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ quarterly and annual real GDP series as published and current in April 2025; true if the most recent published figure at that date showed a contraction of close to 1 percent, false if the then-current figure showed growth or a materially smaller fall.

specificity.statement: I’m proud to say there are 29,000 fewer victims of serious violent crime; there’s a 16 percent reduction in serious youth offending.
specificity.explanation: Two named measures with a count and a percentage attached; a reader can go and check both against the published series.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: If his Government is so supportive of pay equity, how many of the 33 active pay equity claims that were in the process when he became Prime Minister have been settled during his two years as Prime Minister?
specificity.explanation: A precise, checkable question: a named count of claims, a defined start point, and a defined period. As specific as a precise answer would be.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Once fully rolled out, around 130,000 additional women will be eligible for free screening every two years.
specificity.explanation: A quantified consequence of the programme with a stated screening interval — checkable against the programme's own costings.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The changes that we are making, both of a fiscal and a regulatory character, are both short term and medium term.
specificity.explanation: Names no change, no figure, no mechanism and no date; "fiscal and regulatory" and "short and medium term" between them exclude nothing.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I consider that the member who was the education Minister for 5½ years did a pretty bad job, actually, making sure that over half our kids weren't at school regularly and that half of them couldn't read at the standard they needed to be going into high school, and 80 percent weren’t at the standard they needed in maths.
civility.explanation: Largely a criticism of a record, backed with figures, which the re-anchored scale treats as civil — but "did a pretty bad job" is a judgement of the member's personal performance rather than of the policy, so it edges toward the person without landing on them.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: And just look at the front bench across the road. Do you think there are any economically literate people in that front bench? It's unbelievable.
civility.explanation: A direct attack on the intelligence and competence of the members opposite rather than on any argument they have made.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I know you might be worried about your union mates, but actually we're not worried about your unions.
civility.explanation: Imputes to the member personally that he is motivated by loyalty to "union mates" rather than by the public interest — a sneer at motive rather than an engagement with the negotiating position.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Not surprising—can't do math, so not a surprise, but we're actually making it workable given the complexities around that regime, and it's still available for people today, and we encourage unions and members to make claims under the pay equity legislation that's there.
civility.explanation: "Can't do math" is a jibe at the member's personal competence, not a criticism of the costing or the policy.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: So why is he willing to accept a pay rise in line with inflation, claim a $50,000 housing allowance, and spend $44,000 on a helicopter ride so he could take a photograph for his Facebook, while his Government makes pay offers to workers like firefighters, nurses, and teachers that amount to pay cuts in real terms?
civility.explanation: Goes beyond the policy contrast to impute a personal motive — vanity, a photo for his Facebook — which is a sneer at the person rather than at the pay offer being criticised.
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: And just look at the front bench across the road. Do you think there are any economically literate people in that front bench? It's unbelievable.
focus.explanation: Asked whether New Zealanders are better off, the answer turns entirely on what the other side's front bench is like. No policy, measure or figure is named in this passage.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I know you might be worried about your union mates, but actually we're not worried about your unions.
focus.explanation: Responding to a question about pay negotiations, this sentence is entirely about the other side's alliances; no pay offer, settlement or process is named.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: How has refusing to meaningfully negotiate with firefighters, doctors, nurses, and teachers, contributing to what may well be the largest strike action New Zealand's seen in a generation, made things better for New Zealanders?
focus.explanation: Squarely about a live policy matter — the government's conduct of public sector pay negotiations — and names the specific workforces affected rather than attacking the governing parties in general.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: How has scrapping pay equity agreements, therefore cutting the future pay for thousands of New Zealand workers, mostly women, made things better off for New Zealanders?
focus.explanation: Names a specific policy change and the specific outcome attributed to it. This is scrutiny of a named measure, not party-bashing.
focus.subject: speaker

divination.statement: We're now growing now; we're expected to grow even further in quarter four.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that GDP growth in the December 2025 quarter will exceed growth in the current quarter.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ quarterly GDP release for the December 2025 quarter; true if real GDP growth in that quarter is positive and higher than the September 2025 quarter, false if it is lower or negative.

rigor.statement: It has long been a rite of passage for Kiwis to venture overseas.
rigor.explanation: Appeal to tradition: the fact that emigration is long-established is offered as the reason the current outflow needs no answer, but nothing connects the historical pattern to the scale of departures the question raised.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: As is the case with statistics, they’re so backward looking.
rigor.explanation: Dismisses the contradicting data by category rather than by content — that GDP figures describe a past quarter does not show the figure cited was wrong or irrelevant to the claim being defended.
rigor.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Treasury forecast in Budget Economic and Fiscal Update indicated that we would continue, unfortunately, to see jobseeker numbers rise until December.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Budget Economic and Fiscal Update contained a Treasury forecast of rising Jobseeker Support recipient numbers through to December.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury's Budget Economic and Fiscal Update 2025 benefit-recipient projections; true if the Jobseeker Support recipient track is forecast to keep rising to a December 2025 peak, false if the forecast has numbers flat or falling before then.

veracity.statement: We’re also branching out into new areas of research, with $70 million committed to AI technology, $71 million for future materials and magnet technologies, and $42 million to establish a biodiscovery platform, and we’ve more than doubled investment into our fast-growing gaming sector.
veracity.explanation: Asserts three specific funding commitments ($70m AI, $71m future materials and magnets, $42m biodiscovery platform) and that investment in the gaming sector has more than doubled.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2025 appropriations and MBIE science, innovation and technology funding announcements; true if the three named amounts appear as committed for those purposes and the gaming-sector allocation is more than twice its prior level, false if the amounts or the doubling do not match.

veracity.statement: How many of the 200 New Zealanders who leave our shores each day are qualified construction workers?
veracity.explanation: Asserts, as the premise of the question, that around 200 New Zealanders depart the country permanently each day.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ international migration statistics for the most recent 12 months to the statement date; true if departures of New Zealand citizens (or net loss of NZ citizens, on the reading intended) average approximately 200 per day, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: Why is construction activity the lowest it has been since 2019, when he promised more people wearing high-vis and hard hats?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that construction activity is currently at its lowest level since 2019.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ value of building work put in place / building consents series; true if the latest quarter's construction activity is below every quarter since 2019 on the standard measure, false if any intervening period was lower.

veracity.statement: Why did the Government promise more people wearing high-vis and hard hats when there has been $2.9 billion less spent on roads, housing, and hospitals over the past year?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that spending on roads, housing and hospitals fell by $2.9 billion over the past year.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury and agency capital expenditure figures for transport, housing and health infrastructure for the year to the statement date compared with the preceding year; true if the combined reduction is approximately $2.9 billion, false if the aggregate is materially different or rose.

veracity.statement: On the matter of the hospital, it’s this Government that's actually accelerated the delivery of the Dunedin Hospital project.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the current Government has brought forward the delivery of the new Dunedin Hospital relative to the position it inherited.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Health New Zealand and Ministry of Health project timelines for the new Dunedin Hospital, comparing the completion dates published before the change of government with those current at October 2025; true if the delivery date has been brought forward, false if it has slipped or the scope was reduced without an earlier completion date.

specificity.statement: But we’re not sitting around waiting and watching for that to happen, which is why we’ve got 70,000 people in case management, the most effective intervention that is possible.
specificity.explanation: Names a concrete mechanism (case management) and a caseload figure, though 'the most effective intervention that is possible' is an unquantified assertion tacked on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Can the Prime Minister guarantee that Aotearoa will protect 30 percent of our exclusive economic zone by 2030 as committed to under the 2022 global biodiversity framework; if not, why not?
specificity.explanation: Carries a percentage, a deadline and the named framework the commitment sits under; anyone could go and check progress against it.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: How does cutting fishing industry levies, enabling ring-net fishing in high protection areas, and blocking our own proposal to restrict bottom trawling show that his Government is protecting our oceans in the interests of all New Zealanders, rather than the interests of the commercial fishing industry?
specificity.explanation: Three concrete, checkable policy actions rather than a general complaint, though no figures or dates are attached.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Well, again, I’d just say we have a lot of focus on making sure we protect our oceans. We’re part of the blue Pacific ocean initiative that we do through the Pacific Islands Forum, and we continue to play our role in that and meet our obligations there.
specificity.explanation: One named initiative and forum, but no target, area, timeframe or obligation identified — 'a lot of focus' and 'play our role' commit to nothing checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: It’s actually about helping New Zealanders get ahead by lifting the collective living standards of all Kiwis. That’s what our Government’s focused on. That’s why we see huge potential in aquaculture.
specificity.explanation: A string of generic goods — 'get ahead', 'collective living standards', 'huge potential' — with no figure, mechanism or timeframe behind the aquaculture reference.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Research Funding New Zealand will consolidate the fragmented decision-making process we currently have. It will take on the Endeavour Fund, the Marsden Fund, and Strategic Science Investment Fund—currently administered by three separate funding bodies—as well as health research from the Health Research Council.
specificity.explanation: Names the new body, the four funds being absorbed and the administering agencies — a precise, checkable description of the mechanism.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We’re also branching out into new areas of research, with $70 million committed to AI technology, $71 million for future materials and magnet technologies, and $42 million to establish a biodiscovery platform, and we’ve more than doubled investment into our fast-growing gaming sector.
specificity.explanation: Three named research areas each with a dollar figure attached, plus a stated multiple on gaming investment.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: This is about smarter investment in research that grows our economy, protects our environment, and improves New Zealanders’ lives.
specificity.explanation: A list of generic virtues — smarter, grows, protects, improves — with no figure, mechanism or measurable outcome.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: How many of the 200 New Zealanders who leave our shores each day are qualified construction workers?
specificity.explanation: Carries a concrete figure and a specific occupational category, making the question answerable in principle, though the departure figure is asserted rather than sourced.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Why did the Government promise more people wearing high-vis and hard hats when there has been $2.9 billion less spent on roads, housing, and hospitals over the past year?
specificity.explanation: A dollar figure, three named spending areas and a stated period, all checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Can the Prime Minister guarantee that Aotearoa will protect 30 percent of our exclusive economic zone by 2030 as committed to under the 2022 global biodiversity framework; if not, why not?
focus.explanation: Squarely on a named international commitment and a specific marine protection target — accountability for a stated policy obligation, no party framing at all.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: How does cutting fishing industry levies, enabling ring-net fishing in high protection areas, and blocking our own proposal to restrict bottom trawling show that his Government is protecting our oceans in the interests of all New Zealanders, rather than the interests of the commercial fishing industry?
focus.explanation: Names three specific government decisions and tests them against a stated objective; this is scrutiny of policy, not party-bashing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Why is construction activity the lowest it has been since 2019, when he promised more people wearing high-vis and hard hats?
focus.explanation: Names a stated government commitment and sets a measurable outcome against it — the core accountability function, on-policy throughout.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: No doubt their skills are in high demand over in Australian, and if she writes me a letter, I'll consider responding to it.
focus.explanation: Declines to engage the policy question at all; the reply is about how the member should address him rather than about construction workers or emigration.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Once again, this is taking some time because of the dreadful fiscal burden that was left on the current Government due to the profligacy of the period of time between 2020 and 2023.
focus.explanation: Answers a question about infrastructure spending by characterising the previous government's conduct in general terms; no policy, figure or mechanism is named, only the other side's alleged profligacy.
focus.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: What’s more important to his Government: protecting the ability for the industry to harvest the last remaining orange roughy, or protecting the integrity of our vulnerable marine ecosystems?
rigor.explanation: False dichotomy: the question is constructed so that only two mutually exclusive options exist, with nothing offered to establish that the fishery and ecosystem integrity cannot both be pursued.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: What does the Prime Minister think of the implicit suggestion by the questioner that independent Pacific Island nations be told how to use their waters and resources?
rigor.explanation: Strawman: the questions asked were about New Zealand's own exclusive economic zone and marine protected areas, and nothing in them proposed directing other nations' use of their waters; the imputed position is invented and then queried.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: When you create a fiscal perfect storm and the cost of money—interest rates—becomes recklessly high, the Reserve Bank intervenes and increases the cost of money—the interest rate. That has a direct impact on the confidence and the ability of people to fund projects. And therein lies the lesson for that particular member as she struggles to understand economics.
rigor.explanation: There is a real causal chain offered — loose fiscal conditions, Reserve Bank tightening, higher funding costs, weaker construction — and the conclusion does not rest on the insult, so it is scored on the argument. But the middle step is circular (the cost of money becomes high, so the Bank increases the cost of money) and nothing links it to the specific 2019-low figure put to him.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: No doubt their skills are in high demand over in Australian, and if she writes me a letter, I'll consider responding to it.
civility.explanation: Dismisses the questioner rather than the question — telling her to write a letter he may or may not answer is condescension aimed at the member, short of a direct insult.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: When you create a fiscal perfect storm and the cost of money—interest rates—becomes recklessly high, the Reserve Bank intervenes and increases the cost of money—the interest rate. That has a direct impact on the confidence and the ability of people to fund projects. And therein lies the lesson for that particular member as she struggles to understand economics.
civility.explanation: 'as she struggles to understand economics' is a direct attack on the member's competence rather than on her argument.
civility.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We have been running a set of policies that have enabled society to see that we are bringing the books back in order. As matters improve and as the market picks up, who knows what options will be available to us in the future.
specificity.explanation: An answer on apprentice numbers that names no policy, no figure, no mechanism and no timeframe — "a set of policies", "bringing the books back in order", "who knows what options". Nothing here could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Why did he say to New Zealanders that there will be more people wearing hi-vis and hard hats when there has been, under his watch, $2.9 billion less spent on infrastructure and when his Government has cut Apprenticeship Boost for civil engineering, there are 20,000 fewer construction jobs in New Zealand, and 760 construction firms have gone under, under his watch?
specificity.explanation: Four checkable quantities in one question — $2.9 billion, a named scheme (Apprenticeship Boost for civil engineering), 20,000 jobs, 760 firms. A precise question is as specific as a precise answer.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The hope is we will dig our own coal up, starting with 200,000-plus tonnes to reduce our reliance on imported Indonesian coal. The hope is that with the $200 million allocated in the Budget, we will accelerate the development of the oil and gas industry.
specificity.explanation: Two concrete quantities tied to named actions — 200,000-plus tonnes of domestic coal substituting for Indonesian imports, and $200 million of Budget funding for oil and gas development. Missing only timeframes.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: It’s really important that the Minister for Fisheries and Oceans deals in facts, and those facts have to be informed by rationality, science, and technology. Then, when those facts are evident, our society is more than capable of adapting to the challenges.
specificity.explanation: A string of generic virtues — facts, rationality, science, technology, adapting — with no figure, no named measure and no mechanism. Nothing here could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Obviously, setting total allowable commercial catch limits for any fish species is a balance, as reflected in the purpose of the Fisheries Act. Not only do we have to be mindful of the scientific evidence and the pressure on stocks, we also have to take account of the statutory status of utilisation.
specificity.explanation: Names the governing statute and the two statutory considerations that bear on catch limits, which is real content — but supplies no catch figure, no assessment and no date, when the question asked specifically about the orange roughy limits and what had changed.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Over the last 12 months, the strong wool indicator is up 32 percent, mid micron up 41 percent, and fine wool up 35 percent. These are levels not seen in nine years, and much of this increase has occurred in the last few weeks.
specificity.explanation: Three separate price movements with percentages, a stated period, and a historical comparison. Directly checkable against the auction record.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We’ve directed Government departments to prioritise wool and fibres in Government buildings, driving demand and backing our farmers.
specificity.explanation: A named, checkable mechanism — a directive to departments covering wool in government buildings — but no coverage threshold, no value and no date by which it applies.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Why did he say to New Zealanders that there will be more people wearing hi-vis and hard hats when there has been, under his watch, $2.9 billion less spent on infrastructure and when his Government has cut Apprenticeship Boost for civil engineering, there are 20,000 fewer construction jobs in New Zealand, and 760 construction firms have gone under, under his watch?
focus.explanation: Legitimate scrutiny: names a specific ministerial commitment, a named programme and specific outcome figures. Holding a Minister to a stated commitment is on-policy, not tribalism.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: If you want to see what happens when ideology trumps competence, when virtue signalling replaces governing, and when chaos becomes policy, then look no further than the unholy alliance of the Labour - Greens - Te Pāti Māori.
focus.explanation: Names no policy, measure, figure or outcome — the entire content is a characterisation of three opposition parties as a bloc. This is party framing with nothing for anyone to engage with or check.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Why did he say to New Zealanders that there will be more people wearing hi-vis and hard hats when there has been, under his watch, $2.9 billion less spent on infrastructure and when his Government has cut Apprenticeship Boost for civil engineering, there are 20,000 fewer construction jobs in New Zealand, and 760 construction firms have gone under, under his watch?
veracity.explanation: Asserts four factual claims about the present government's record: infrastructure spend down $2.9b, Apprenticeship Boost cut for civil engineering, 20,000 fewer construction jobs, 760 construction firm failures.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury/Infrastructure Commission capital expenditure series for the periods compared (true if the fall is ~$2.9b); TEC/MSD Apprenticeship Boost eligibility settings (true if civil engineering was removed); Stats NZ HLFS construction employment change since late 2023 (true if ~20,000 fewer); NZ Companies Office / Centrix construction liquidation counts (true if ~760 in the period). False if any figure is materially different from these sources.

veracity.statement: But I have to tell the member that 5.2 million people residing in the South Pacific with an economy of about $440 billion Kiwi dollars have zero control over the direction or the heat being generated by the Pacific Ocean.
veracity.explanation: Asserts two quantities about New Zealand — a population of 5.2 million and an economy of about NZ$440 billion.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ estimated resident population at the date of the statement (true if ~5.2m) and Stats NZ nominal GDP for the year to mid-2025 (true if ~NZ$440b). False if either is materially outside those values.

veracity.statement: Obviously, our contribution to global emissions is 0.17 percent—less than 1 percent!
veracity.explanation: Asserts New Zealand's share of global greenhouse gas emissions is 0.17 percent.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry for the Environment's New Zealand Greenhouse Gas Inventory share-of-global figure, cross-checked against the Global Carbon Budget / EDGAR national shares: true if NZ's share is ~0.17% of global gross emissions, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: With respect to mining fossils, which is what four countries are doing—namely, China, USA, India, and Russia—and contributing to 60 percent of the emissions, what hope have we got to change that?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that China, the USA, India and Russia together account for 60 percent of emissions.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Global Carbon Project / EDGAR national shares of global CO2 emissions for the most recent reported year: true if the four countries' combined share is ~60%, false if materially below or above (e.g. under 50% or over 70%).

veracity.statement: The hope is we will dig our own coal up, starting with 200,000-plus tonnes to reduce our reliance on imported Indonesian coal. The hope is that with the $200 million allocated in the Budget, we will accelerate the development of the oil and gas industry.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that $200 million was allocated in the Budget for accelerating oil and gas development.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2025 documents (Vote Business, Science and Innovation / energy appropriations): true if an appropriation of approximately $200 million for gas or oil field development or co-investment appears, false if no such allocation exists or the amount is materially different.

veracity.statement: Over the last 12 months, the strong wool indicator is up 32 percent, mid micron up 41 percent, and fine wool up 35 percent. These are levels not seen in nine years, and much of this increase has occurred in the last few weeks.
veracity.explanation: Asserts specific 12-month price rises for three wool categories and that current levels are the highest in nine years.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: PGG Wrightson / NZ Wool Services weekly auction indicators for strong wool, mid micron and fine wool: true if the 12-month changes to October 2025 are approximately +32%, +41% and +35% and the levels exceed any since 2016, false if the movements are materially different or higher levels occurred within the last nine years.

veracity.statement: Nanjing is a major hub for the international wool-textile trade, and China accounts for approximately 40 percent of New Zealand’s wool exports.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that China takes approximately 40 percent of New Zealand's wool exports.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ overseas merchandise trade statistics, wool exports by destination for the most recent full year: true if China's share is approximately 40% by value or volume, false if materially different.

rigor.statement: I repeat: once inflation runs rampant, this is the devastating impact that inflationary policies have upon the confidence of investors, the ability of firms, and, quite frankly, it shrinks the options that New Zealanders have.
rigor.explanation: Offers inflation as the cause of the construction figures put to him, but supplies no link between the two — no timing, no magnitude, no mechanism connecting past inflation to the specific job and firm-failure numbers. The conclusion (that these figures are inherited inflationary damage) is asserted rather than derived.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: It is the height of conceit to imagine that somehow by closing down New Zealand industry we’re going to save the planet. The planet is more than capable of saving itself and we will adapt in good time.
rigor.explanation: Strawman plus false dichotomy: the question asked whether drilling for more fossil fuels helps or harms, not whether New Zealand should close down its industry to "save the planet" single-handedly. The conclusion (no action warranted) rests on refuting a position nobody advanced, and "the planet is more than capable of saving itself" is asserted with nothing offered in support.
rigor.subject: speaker

divination.statement: On the question of hard hats and high-vis, I can assure you coal mining is about to improve those statistics.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that expansion of coal mining will raise employment in hi-vis/hard-hat (construction and extractive) work. Not a promise about his own action — it is a claim about a labour-market outcome.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ / MBIE employment figures for coal mining and the wider mining sector: true if mining employment rises measurably above its 2025 level within the stated horizon; false if it is flat or falls.

divination.statement: On the question of fisheries, the proposed mining, God willing, to proceed off the coast of Taranaki will have minimal impact on the strength or the vitality of fisheries.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that the proposed seabed mining off Taranaki will have minimal effect on fish stocks. A claim about a future environmental outcome, not a promise about his own action.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Fisheries NZ stock assessments and monitoring for the affected South Taranaki Bight stocks after mining commences, plus any EPA/consent monitoring reports: true if no decline in stock status or catch attributable to the mining is recorded, false if monitoring identifies a material adverse effect on the stocks.

civility.statement: Sadly, we are unlikely to see unanimity until the former Minister disappears from Parliament.
civility.explanation: Not an argument about a policy — a personal jab at an identifiable member, expressing the wish that they leave Parliament. It lands on the person rather than on any position they hold.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: If you want to see what happens when ideology trumps competence, when virtue signalling replaces governing, and when chaos becomes policy, then look no further than the unholy alliance of the Labour - Greens - Te Pāti Māori.
civility.explanation: Blunt and hostile, but aimed at parties collectively rather than at any individual member; no person's character, competence or worth is attacked. The tribalism is caught by Focus, not here.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Well, either that man doesn’t know how to count, being a former Minister of Education, or, quite simply, Mr Hipkins is so committed to trying to do a deal that he’ll do anything to try to get into Government.
civility.explanation: A direct attack on Hipkins the person — mocking his numeracy with a jab at his record as Education Minister, then imputing unprincipled desperation. Neither half engages a policy.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Damien O’Connor and his thugging mate of David Parker were beating up rural New Zealand.
civility.explanation: Names two members and calls one a 'thug'. The characterisation lands on the individuals' character, not on the emissions policy being contested.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I came here, after spending 30 years in a cowshed—and I know that that member hasn’t spent three—saying that I would fight for the rights of rural people.
civility.explanation: A pointed dig at another member's lack of farming experience. It edges onto the person's standing rather than their argument, but stops short of an insult about their character or competence.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Well, either that man doesn’t know how to count, being a former Minister of Education, or, quite simply, Mr Hipkins is so committed to trying to do a deal that he’ll do anything to try to get into Government.
rigor.explanation: A false dichotomy: the two offered options (innumeracy or unprincipled ambition) are presented as exhaustive when a flippant answer to a coalition question supports neither.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: You cannot trust Labour when it comes to health.
rigor.explanation: Hasty generalisation: a single undelivered 2017 commitment is taken to establish a blanket conclusion about trustworthiness across an entire policy domain.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I stood up because I believe in farmers, and I am a farmer myself.
rigor.explanation: Offered as a rebuttal to the accusation of being lobbied, but asserting one's own sincerity and credentials does not bear on whether lobbying occurred — the conclusion does not follow from the premise.
rigor.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: This is the same Chris Hipkins who said he’ll work with anyone—anyone—if it means a sniff of the Treasury benches.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Hipkins has publicly stated he would work with any party in order to form a government.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Public record of Hipkins' statements on coalition partners in 2024–2025 (press conferences, interviews, Hansard). True if he stated he would work with any party without exclusion; false if he ruled any party out (e.g. NZ First or ACT) over that period.

veracity.statement: For the first time in two years, we had a question about the environment!
veracity.explanation: Asserts that no question about the environment had been asked (by the Green Party) in the House for two years before this day.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Hansard oral and written question records for the two years to 15 October 2025. True if no Green Party question on an environmental subject appears in that window; false if any does.

veracity.statement: We’ve got spending under control, inflation down to 2.7 percent, and mortgage rates cut eight times.
veracity.explanation: Asserts an annual inflation rate of 2.7 percent as the current figure, and that mortgage/official interest rates have been cut on eight occasions under this government.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ Consumers Price Index annual rate for the most recent quarter published before 15 October 2025, and the RBNZ record of Official Cash Rate decisions since the government took office. True if the CPI print is 2.7% and the count of OCR cuts is eight; false if either is materially different.

veracity.statement: We’re reducing wait-lists for hips, knees and cataracts, all of which went up under Chris Hipkins when he was Minister of Health.
veracity.explanation: Two factual assertions: that planned-care waiting lists for hip, knee and cataract procedures are currently falling, and that they rose during Hipkins' tenure as Minister of Health.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Te Whatu Ora planned care waiting list data for hip replacement, knee replacement and cataract surgery. True if the counts fell over 2024–2025 and rose across Hipkins' term as Health Minister (2020–2022); false if either direction is reversed.

veracity.statement: We’ve delivered 33 new cancer medicines, delivered the biggest funding boost for general practitioners, and just today announced an extension to breast screening, which, by the way, Labour promised in 2017 with their coalition agreement with New Zealand First but failed to deliver.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a count of 33 newly funded cancer medicines, a record GP funding increase, and that the 2017 Labour–NZ First coalition agreement contained an undelivered breast-screening extension commitment.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Pharmac's record of cancer medicines funded since late 2023 (true if 33 or more); the text of the 2017 Labour–New Zealand First coalition agreement (true if it contains a breast screening extension commitment); and BreastScreen Aotearoa eligibility as at 2023 (true if the extension had not been implemented).

veracity.statement: Now, David Seymour was the only guy in this entire precinct that voted against the zero carbon Act.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Seymour cast the sole vote against the Climate Change Response (Zero Carbon) Amendment Bill.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The division record for the third reading of the Climate Change Response (Zero Carbon) Amendment Bill (2019). True if Seymour is recorded as the only member voting against; false if any other member did, or if he did not.

veracity.statement: It’s all doom and gloom and the world is burning—I mean, I’ve heard Arena Williams say that the world is literally burning.
veracity.explanation: Relays a statement attributed to another member — that Arena Williams said the world is literally burning. The accuracy at issue is whether she said it.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: Hansard and public record of Arena Williams' remarks. True if she is recorded saying the world is literally burning (or words to that effect); false if no such statement exists and the attribution is a characterisation.

veracity.statement: Farmers in rural New Zealand are worth almost $60 billion—60 billion—and Chris Hipkins knows this, as the leader of that party.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that farming in New Zealand is worth close to $60 billion. What is being measured — export revenue, GDP contribution or asset value — is left open.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MPI Situation and Outlook for Primary Industries export revenue, and Stats NZ agriculture GDP contribution, for 2024/25. True if a standard published measure of farming's value is close to $60 billion; false if every such measure is materially different.

veracity.statement: It’s a damnable shame that here we are and we are talking about a gas that decays back to carbon dioxide, and it is, factually, two parts per million.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that atmospheric methane is present at a concentration of two parts per million, and that it breaks down into carbon dioxide.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NOAA/NIWA global mean atmospheric methane concentration for 2025, and standard atmospheric chemistry on methane oxidation. True if the concentration rounds to about 2 ppm and methane oxidises to CO2; false if the figure is off by an order of magnitude or the decay pathway is misstated.

focus.statement: It’s like they’ve just remembered that they’re actually called the Green Party.
focus.explanation: Entirely about the other party's identity and priorities. No policy, measure, figure or outcome is named — mockery of a party rather than engagement with anything it has done.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: We’ve delivered 33 new cancer medicines, delivered the biggest funding boost for general practitioners, and just today announced an extension to breast screening, which, by the way, Labour promised in 2017 with their coalition agreement with New Zealand First but failed to deliver.
focus.explanation: Names specific measures — a medicines count, a GP funding decision, a breast screening extension — and holds an opponent to a specific named commitment from a specific agreement. Accountability against a named policy, not party-bashing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: You cannot trust Labour when it comes to health.
focus.explanation: The conclusion drops the named policy and lands on a general character judgement of the other party. Almost no policy content survives in the statement itself.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: The contrast couldn’t be clearer: on that side of the House, chaos, coups, budget blowouts, selective outrage, internal warfare, parties that can’t even organise a press conference without imploding; and on this side, delivery for New Zealanders on the issues that matter.
focus.explanation: A list of the opposition's internal states — coups, warfare, a botched press conference — set against an unnamed 'delivery'. No specific policy, measure, figure or outcome on either side of the contrast.
focus.subject: speaker

divination.statement: Whether it’s a savings tax, whether it’s a property tax, whether it’s a death tax, New Zealanders can be guaranteed that, behind the scenes, that’s what they’re cooking up to take to the next election.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that the Labour/Greens/Te Pāti Māori bloc will take a new savings, property or estate tax to the 2026 general election. It is a prediction about opponents' future conduct, not a promise about the speaker's own action.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: The published 2026 general election tax policies of Labour, the Green Party and Te Pāti Māori. True if at least one of a savings tax, a property/capital tax or an estate ('death') tax appears in those policies; false if none of the three parties campaigns on any of them.

specificity.statement: We’ve got spending under control, inflation down to 2.7 percent, and mortgage rates cut eight times.
specificity.explanation: Carries a named rate and a count — both checkable against published series. Only 'spending under control' is unquantified.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We came to fix what matters, and we are fixing what matters. We are restoring rural confidence.
specificity.explanation: 'What matters' is never named, and 'restoring rural confidence' commits to no mechanism, figure or timeframe. Nothing here could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Two years ago today, Christopher Luxon stood in front of New Zealanders and he made a promise: his promise was that he was going to lower the cost of living and fix the economy. Two years on, it is abundantly clear he has failed to do both of those things.
civility.explanation: Hard criticism aimed squarely at a named commitment and the record against it; no attack on Luxon's character, competence or person.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Instead you left us with an utter mess and you left house owners in a terrible situation, paying interest rates they shouldn’t have been paying, because of your behaviour as the Government that then sat around spending New Zealanders’ money, borrowing money for New Zealanders to pay so that New Zealand is now paying interest every single year that is more than Corrections, Police, and Defence, and our fire service all together because of him and his former Government.
civility.explanation: Pointed and personalised — "your behaviour", "because of him" — but the charge is about his record in office (spending and borrowing decisions) rather than his character or competence as a person.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I’ve no idea why that woman keeps shouting.
civility.explanation: A dismissive personal jibe at another member — refusing to name her, reducing her contribution to "shouting". Aimed at the person, not at anything she argued.
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Two years ago today, Christopher Luxon stood in front of New Zealanders and he made a promise: his promise was that he was going to lower the cost of living and fix the economy. Two years on, it is abundantly clear he has failed to do both of those things.
focus.explanation: Names a specific commitment (lower the cost of living, fix the economy) and measures the Government against it. This is accountability, not party-bashing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: It shows that they have no plan. They know they can’t defend their own record; they know they don’t know how to fix the mess that they have been creating; all they can do is scaremonger and attack, because they don’t know how to turn things around.
focus.explanation: Entirely about the other party's supposed motives and inner state. No policy, measure, figure or outcome is named.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: At the same time, war has broken out in Te Pāti Māori. Perhaps they should get President Trump to come and negotiate for them and be the facilitator.
focus.explanation: Entirely about another party's internal divisions, played for a joke. No policy, measure, figure or outcome is named.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: We’ve released this defence industry strategy, so our New Zealand businesses like Syos, like Dawn Aerospace, like Kea Aerospace, like all the businesses up and down the country who are currently manufacturing for people like Rocket Lab and others, so that they are actually going to be able to work with the Defence Force to help provide aerial drones, land drones, and sea drones for our New Zealand Defence Force.
focus.explanation: Squarely on the mechanism of a named policy — who it involves and what it is meant to produce. No party framing at all.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Increasing unemployment; an economy that’s shrinking; more kids living in poverty; more people homeless and living on the streets; the construction sector—remember, they were going to get things done and get things building again—is at its lowest point in seven years, two years into this Government’s leadership; $3 billion less spending on building stuff in the last year compared to when they became the Government.
specificity.explanation: Carries checkable content: a named sector at a stated multi-year low, a dollar figure ($3 billion) and a stated comparison period. Precision, not truth, is what is scored here.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We will be focused on jobs, on health, on homes, on real action on the cost of living—not more broken promises, more blame, and more excuses, which is all this Government has to offer.
specificity.explanation: A list of policy areas with no mechanism, figure, target or timeframe attached — nothing here could be checked or acted on. The surrounding passage supplies no detail either.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We’ve released this defence industry strategy, so our New Zealand businesses like Syos, like Dawn Aerospace, like Kea Aerospace, like all the businesses up and down the country who are currently manufacturing for people like Rocket Lab and others, so that they are actually going to be able to work with the Defence Force to help provide aerial drones, land drones, and sea drones for our New Zealand Defence Force.
specificity.explanation: Names the policy document, four specific firms and three concrete capability classes (aerial, land and sea drones). Falls short of 1.0 because no funding figure, procurement volume or timeframe is attached.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Increasing unemployment; an economy that’s shrinking; more kids living in poverty; more people homeless and living on the streets; the construction sector—remember, they were going to get things done and get things building again—is at its lowest point in seven years, two years into this Government’s leadership; $3 billion less spending on building stuff in the last year compared to when they became the Government.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a compound set of present-state facts: unemployment rising, GDP contracting, child poverty and homelessness rising, construction activity at a seven-year low, and $3bn less capital/building spend in the last year than at the change of government.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ HLFS unemployment rate and quarterly GDP series for 2024-25 (true if unemployment rose and GDP contracted over the period); Stats NZ child poverty statistics release; MSD/HUD emergency and transitional housing and rough-sleeping counts; Stats NZ building consents/construction activity series (true if the seven-year-low characterisation holds); Treasury/Budget capital expenditure on building in the latest full year versus 2023. False if any of the named indicators moved the other way.

veracity.statement: There is one thing the Government has broken records on, and that is the number of New Zealanders giving up and leaving.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that departures of New Zealanders under this Government are at an all-time record level.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ international migration statistics, permanent and long-term departures of New Zealand citizens (annual series). True if the annual figure for a year under this Government is the highest on record; false if an earlier year exceeds it.

veracity.statement: Every time a member on the opposite side of the House gets on a plane to fly to Auckland or to Christchurch, I want them to think of one thing: the number of people on that plane is the equivalent number of people who are permanently leaving the country every day—every day—under their Government’s leadership.
veracity.explanation: A quantified analogy: that permanent departures from New Zealand currently run at roughly one domestic jet-load of people per day.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ permanent and long-term departures of New Zealand citizens for the most recent 12 months, divided by 365, compared with the seat capacity of the jets flown on main-trunk domestic routes (roughly 170–300 seats). True if the daily figure falls in that band; false if it is materially below or above it.

veracity.statement: Instead you left us with an utter mess and you left house owners in a terrible situation, paying interest rates they shouldn’t have been paying, because of your behaviour as the Government that then sat around spending New Zealanders’ money, borrowing money for New Zealanders to pay so that New Zealand is now paying interest every single year that is more than Corrections, Police, and Defence, and our fire service all together because of him and his former Government.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Crown's annual finance costs (debt-servicing) now exceed the combined annual appropriations for Corrections, Police, Defence and Fire and Emergency New Zealand.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury Budget 2025 / Financial Statements of the Government: core Crown finance costs for the year, compared against the summed appropriations for Vote Corrections, Vote Police, Vote Defence plus Vote Defence Force, and FENZ funding. True if finance costs are the larger figure; false if the combined votes exceed them.

veracity.statement: We see interest rates dropping.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that interest rates in New Zealand are falling as at October 2025.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: RBNZ Official Cash Rate track and retail mortgage rate series over the 12 months to October 2025. True if the OCR and advertised mortgage rates are materially lower than a year earlier; false if flat or rising.

veracity.statement: Despite what the left say, we have the fourth largest search and rescue area in the world.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific ranking: that New Zealand's search and rescue region is the fourth largest of any country's.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Maritime New Zealand / RCCNZ published area of New Zealand's search and rescue region, ranked against the declared SRR areas of other states in IMO/ICAO SAR documentation. True if New Zealand ranks fourth; false if it ranks materially higher or lower.

rigor.statement: It shows that they have no plan. They know they can’t defend their own record; they know they don’t know how to fix the mess that they have been creating; all they can do is scaremonger and attack, because they don’t know how to turn things around.
rigor.explanation: Non sequitur plus mind-reading: from the observation that the Health Minister mentioned Labour early in a speech, the conclusion that the Government has no plan and privately knows it cannot defend its record does not follow. Nothing is offered to bridge the two.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I would say to Chris Hipkins that, well, if you’re going to do all these things, mate, then how come you didn’t do it in the six years that you were there?
rigor.explanation: Tu quoque. That the speaker's opponent did not do something in office bears on his consistency, not on whether the proposal is now sound; nothing is offered against the proposal itself.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: That’s why they’re going because New Zealand, in the last six years of the Labour Government, decided to cut the mines.
rigor.explanation: Asserted causation with nothing offered to support it: a single cause (mining policy under the previous government) is declared to explain why New Zealanders are moving to Australia, with no evidence linking emigration flows to that policy and no alternative explanations addressed.
rigor.subject: speaker

divination.statement: We’ve already started the Indian free-trade agreement negotiations, and we will get there, and we’ll get there in this term.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that New Zealand and India will conclude a free-trade agreement before the end of the current parliamentary term — an outcome that depends on the Indian government as well as New Zealand's.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: MFAT trade agreement records. True if a New Zealand–India FTA is concluded or signed before the 2026 general election; false if negotiations remain unconcluded at that point.

rigor.statement: They have two options: put their prices up or close their doors.
rigor.explanation: False dichotomy: the claim that practices face exactly two options excludes obvious alternatives (absorbing costs, changing service mix, reducing hours, adding other charges — which she herself describes later in the speech). The conclusion is asserted rather than supported.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: If the Government wants to dismiss that this is a problem, that is only proof of how out of touch they are.
